facts.fact: Adwave's guide says foot-traffic-driving CTV campaigns concentrate 80-90% of impressions within the real customer drive radius, typically 5-12 miles for local retailers and restaurants.
facts.quote: Foot traffic-driving campaigns concentrate 80-90% of impressions in the real customer drive radius (typically 5-12 miles for most local retailers and restaurants).

facts.fact: Adwave's guide recommends a frequency of 3-5 for foot-traffic CTV campaigns, stating that frequency below 2 does not drive recall and frequency above 7 over-saturates converted households.
facts.quote: Frequency below 2 doesn't drive recall; frequency above 7 over-saturates already-converted households.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide recommends counting weekly foot traffic for 4-6 weeks before a CTV campaign launches to establish a pre/post baseline.
facts.quote: Count weekly foot traffic for 4-6 weeks before the campaign launches.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide reports a typical foot traffic lift of 15-30% for local retailers in well-targeted CTV campaigns at $1,500-$2,500 per month spend within a 5-10 mile drive radius.
facts.quote: Typical foot traffic lift of 15-30% during well-targeted CTV campaigns at $1,500-$2,500/month spend, in a 5-10 mile drive radius.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide reports a typical foot traffic lift of 12-25% for full-service restaurants during CTV campaigns, with the largest gains in Friday-Sunday dinner traffic.
facts.quote: Typical foot traffic lift of 12-25% during CTV campaigns, with the largest gains in dinner traffic Friday-Sunday.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide reports a lift of 8-20% in foot traffic for quick-service restaurants and cafes, with stronger weekday than weekend lift.
facts.quote: Lift of 8-20%, with stronger weekday lift than weekend lift because the decision is more routine.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide reports that intro-class signups at fitness studios typically lift 25-45% during well-targeted CTV campaigns.
facts.quote: Intro-class signups (the foot-traffic equivalent for studios) typically lift 25-45% during well-targeted campaigns.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide reports a service appointment lift of 12-25% for auto services during CTV campaigns.
facts.quote: Service appointment lift of 12-25%, with stronger lift for seasonal services

facts.fact: Adwave's guide reports an in-home estimate appointment lift of 15-35% for home services during CTV campaigns.
facts.quote: In-home visit (estimate appointment) lift of 15-35% during campaigns

facts.fact: Adwave's guide says benchmark ranges assume a 60-90 day campaign window for accurate measurement.
facts.quote: 60-90 day campaign window for accurate measurement

facts.fact: Adwave's guide advises contacting platform support to tighten targeting if more than 20-25% of impressions land outside the real drive radius during weeks 3-4.
facts.quote: If more than 20-25% of impressions are landing outside your real drive radius, contact platform support to tighten targeting.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide, published May 29, 2026, is the source of these CTV foot traffic benchmarks and recommendations.
AdWave's guidance treats a 12-week total foot traffic lift of 15% or more over pre-campaign baseline as strong lift, where the campaign should be kept at current spend or scaled modestly.
facts.quote: **Strong lift (15%+):** Keep campaign at current spend or scale modestly. Foot traffic lift is real and the campaign is paying for itself.

facts.fact: AdWave's guidance treats a foot traffic lift between 5% and 15% as moderate lift, recommending creative or targeting adjustments and another 60-day cycle.
facts.quote: **Moderate lift (5-15%):** Adjust creative or targeting and run another 60-day cycle.

facts.fact: AdWave's guidance treats a foot traffic lift under 5% as weak lift that should be diagnosed before the campaign is pulled.
facts.quote: **Weak lift (under 5%):** Diagnose. Most often the issue is geographic leakage, weak creative, or under-frequency.

facts.fact: According to AdWave, branded search for a business name during a CTV campaign will typically rise 15-40% over baseline.
facts.quote: Searches for your business name during the campaign window will typically rise 15-40% over baseline.

facts.fact: According to AdWave, direct website traffic typically rises 10-25% during a CTV campaign.
facts.quote: Visitors typing your URL directly will typically rise 10-25%.

facts.fact: According to AdWave, Google Business Profile views and direction requests often lift 20-50% during active CTV campaigns.
facts.quote: Views and direction requests on your GBP often lift 20-50% during active CTV campaigns.

facts.fact: According to AdWave, phone call volume for categories where calls are common often lifts 15-35% during CTV campaigns.
facts.quote: call volume often lifts 15-35% during campaigns.

facts.fact: AdWave states that retail campaigns in the four highest-yield seasonal windows typically see 1.5-2x the foot traffic lift of off-season campaigns.
facts.quote: Campaigns running in these windows typically see 1.5-2x the foot traffic lift of off-season campaigns.

facts.fact: AdWave recommends collecting 4-6 weeks of pre-campaign foot traffic data as a baseline before launching a campaign.
facts.quote: Without 4-6 weeks of pre-campaign foot traffic data, you can't measure the lift.

facts.fact: AdWave says foot traffic lift typically builds across 4-8 weeks, so two-week judgments produce false negatives.
facts.quote: Foot traffic lift builds across 4-8 weeks as viewers move from "first impression" to "this is a real place I might visit"

facts.fact: AdWave advises planning for at least a 60-day window before evaluating a CTV foot traffic campaign, ideally 75-90 days.
facts.quote: Plan for at least a 60-day window before evaluating performance, ideally 75-90 days for a clean read.

facts.fact: AdWave states that subscription-tier CTV platforms offer entry points of $50-$500, with most local foot-traffic campaigns running $1,000-$2,500 per month.
facts.quote: Subscription-tier platforms have made CTV accessible at $50-$500 entry points, with most local foot-traffic campaigns running in the $1,000-$2,500/month range.

facts.fact: AdWave states that CTV works best for single-location businesses with a defined drive radius of 3-12 miles.
facts.quote: CTV works best for businesses with a defined drive radius (3-12 miles for most single-location businesses).

facts.fact: AdWave gives the example of a business with a 10-mile real drive radius, noting that a 25-mile targeting radius wastes impressions on viewers who won't visit.
facts.quote: A 25-mile radius for a business with a 10-mile real drive radius wastes impressions on viewers who won't visit.

facts.fact: AdWave's example of a viewer-facing CTA for a foot traffic campaign is 'Visit us this weekend at [address]' rather than a generic 'Learn more at our website.'
facts.quote: "Visit us this weekend at [address]" beats "Learn more at our website."
